blocks.title: Oxidation number
blocks.text: Oxidation numbers, also called oxidation states, are numbers given to each atom or ion in a compound that show its degree of oxidation. They can be positive, negative or zero, and the + or - sign must always be included. The oxidation number is the apparent charge on an atom (per atom) of an element in a molecule or an ion.
A higher positive oxidation number means that an atom or ion is more oxidised; a higher negative oxidation number means that it is more reduced.
